first.rationale: The onboarding decline is the clearest proximal constraint and prior evidence indicates simplification improved completion, time-to-value, and adoption. Verify that evidence against pricing and activation-messaging records before committing, with qualified revenue and downstream retention guardrails because easier onboarding could increase low-quality activation.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified record shows a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding decline while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Activation messaging is a credible alternative but had a smaller retention gain. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% retention decline and failure at first renewal.
